title: U.S. House · Florida's 24th District
area: Parts of Miami-Dade and Broward counties, including Miami Gardens, Opa-locka, North Miami, Carol City and portions of Hollywood and Pembroke Pines.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Frederica S. Wilson did not make the ballot in the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary. Miami-Dade County Commissioner Oliver Gilbert won that primary with 34.4% of the vote (20,131 votes) over state Sen. Shevrin Jones (32.0%) and five other candidates. The Republican primary was canceled and Te Brown advanced unopposed. Patricia Gonzalez is running as a write-in, No Party Affiliation candidate.

candidates.name: Oliver Gilbert
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 34.4% of the vote.

summary.text: Oliver Gilbert is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Florida's 24th District, running to succeed retiring Rep. Frederica Wilson. He currently serves on the Miami-Dade County Commission and previously served as mayor of Miami Gardens.

background.text: Born August 15, 1972, in Miami Gardens, Florida. Received a B.A. in Criminal Justice from Florida A&M University and a J.D. from the University of Miami School of Law.
Worked as a legislative aide to then-state Rep. Dorothy Bendross-Mindingall after law school, then as a prosecutor and in private legal practice.
Was appointed to the Miami Gardens city council in 2008 and elected mayor of Miami Gardens in 2012, serving as the city's second African-American mayor.
Elected to the Miami-Dade County Commission (District 1) in 2020, defeating Sybrina Fulton, and has served since November 17, 2020.

record.text: Currently serves as Miami-Dade County Commissioner for District 1, a role he has held since November 2020; he did not seek re-election to that seat in 2026 in order to run for Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Gilbert has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and his campaign website is a JavaScript-rendered single-page site that returned no readable policy text when fetched; no stated legislative priorities or issue positions could be sourced as of this research. His public record here reflects only his current county-commission role, since Congressional votes/bills will not exist until he takes office.

candidates.name: Te Brown
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Republican primary, unopposed.

summary.text: Te Brown is the Republican nominee for Florida's 24th Congressional District. She describes herself as a real estate developer, small businesswoman and homeschooling mother running as a conservative political outsider.

background.text: Says she grew up in Chicago and built a real estate development and small business career from a young age.
Describes herself as a homeschooling mother.

priorities.text: Housing affordability: redirecting federal housing dollars from long-term rental subsidies toward helping low-income families in the district buy their first home.
School choice: shifting federal education dollars to follow individual students so families can choose public, charter, private or homeschool options.

Immigration enforcement paired with a lawful process for some long-term residents, including an earned path to citizenship for Haitian Temporary Protected Status holders who meet a work-history, tax-payment and clean-record standard.

positions.summary: Supports directing federal education dollars to follow students rather than school systems, so families can choose public, charter, private or homeschool options.
positions.quote: Te Brown supports taking federal education dollars that currently prop up failing schools and putting that money directly in the hands of parents by funding students, not systems.

positions.summary: Supports securing the border, enforcing immigration law, and prioritizing removal of people who pose a public-safety threat, while also supporting an earned path to citizenship for longtime Haitian TPS holders in South Florida.

candidates.researchNotes: Te Brown has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions are drawn from her campaign website's issues page. She has not previously held elected office, so has no official voting or bill-sponsorship record.

candidates.name: Patricia Gonzalez
candidates.ballotNote: Certified write-in candidate (No Party Affiliation); voters must write in her name to vote for her.

summary.text: Patricia Gonzalez is a certified write-in, No Party Affiliation candidate for Florida's 24th Congressional District. She works as a mortgage broker and describes her positions as Republican-leaning while running without party affiliation.

background.text: Has run for this same seat previously, including a withdrawn 2022 primary bid and a 2024 primary loss, before qualifying as a write-in candidate for 2026.

priorities.text: Protecting the Constitution and the separation of powers among the presidency, Congress and the Supreme Court.
Making homeownership simpler by reducing regulatory barriers and costs for working Americans.
Supporting legal, orderly immigration, with a lawful path to remain for non-criminal residents while applying immigration consequences to serious felony convictions.

positions.summary: Supports legal, orderly immigration and says people who have built their lives in America and are not serious criminals should have a lawful opportunity to remain, while serious felony convictions should carry immigration consequences.
positions.quote: Support legal, orderly immigration. People who have built their lives in America and are not serious criminals should have a lawful opportunity to remain, while serious felony convictions should have immigration consequences consistent with federal law and due process.

positions.summary: Says she would protect Medicare for those who depend on it while opposing a government-run Medicare for All system.
positions.quote: Protect Medicare for those who depend on it while opposing a government-run Medicare-for-All system.

positions.summary: Describes herself as pro-life and says she stands for the protection of unborn children.
positions.quote: Stand for the protection of unborn children.

positions.summary: Supports Israel's right to exist and defend itself and says she would maintain a strong U.S.-Israel relationship.
positions.quote: Support Israel's right to exist and defend itself and maintain a strong U.S.-Israel relationship.

candidates.researchNotes: As a write-in candidate, Gonzalez has minimal public footprint beyond her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers; no campaign website content beyond a contact link was located.
